pages.title: How this site was made: Mistral, a European brain
pages.description: How this site was made: by agents, in which sessions, from which sources, with signed commits.
pages.text:
How this site was made
 How this site was made
 By agents, from one article and Mistral’s own pages, on 20 November 2026. Everything that made it is public, so you can check it.
 The request
 The site began as one request in the Sovereign Website factory: SovereignWebsite__Factory/requests , from the site template the factory seeds. Its brief is Dinis Cruz’s article A European brain for a sovereign website , published on 20 November 2026.
 The agents and their sessions
 conductor.mistral@SovereignWebsite.dinis : the conductor, who split the work, set the rules and assembles the site. Session: claude.ai/code/session_01Kw9UwFkZvAwG1yRZJhexqX .
 The site agent, working for the conductor in the same session: the content, the five designs, the share card and the checks.
 The research agent: Mistral’s facts, each checked on Mistral’s own pages, with its source, a verbatim quote and the date it was read, including where Mistral’s pages differ from the article.
 The demo agent: the demos at /demos/ . Its calls to Mistral, with their tokens, are on the sources page .
 The agents that work on this site are listed in data/agents.json . Each signs its commits with a key published at agents.sovereignweb.site , and adds Agent: and Claude-Session: trailers, as the repository’s rules require.
 The rules they worked under
 Never invent a fact, a price, a benchmark, a customer or a quote. Every fact links its source and says when it was read.
 Quotes from the article are short, verbatim, attributed and linked.
 The partnership is a proposal: nothing has been agreed with Mistral. Pi and tablet performance is an estimate, not measured.
 No Mistral logo, wordmark or brand colours. Static files only, no cookies, no tracking, no inline script or style, no CDN.
 Sources
 Every source, with the date it was read, is on the sources page .
 Every change
 The commits : who changed what, and when, each signed.
 The workflow runs : each publish of the site, with its checks (links, em dashes, leak scan, HTML validity, accessibility, link previews).
 Design rounds
 Five designs were made from the same facts, each a rebuild; compare them . Each design round and its review is in the design agent’s back office .
 Synthetic user runs
 Runs of synthetic users against this site, and what they found, are listed here as the site’s agents record them. None yet.

Then answer my questions about Mistral, a European brain for a sovereign website, with a link for each point,
and say plainly when the site does not say something.

I want to change: [describe the change].

pages.title: A European brain: demos
pages.description: Working demonstrations, in your browser, of a sovereign website whose AI model is the owner's choice, like the host.
pages.text:
Demos, London, 21 November 2026
 The model is a choice the owner makes, like the host
 A sovereign website's files are yours, and you can move them to any host. These demos show the same for its brain: one standard way of calling a model, and the owner picks what sits behind it, on the device, in Europe, or anywhere, with their own key.
 This is the claim of A European brain for a sovereign website by Dinis Cruz: if the model can only ever be one provider, the site is sovereign in its files and rented in its brain. Here you can try it rather than read about it. Everything runs in your browser; there is no server of ours, and nothing is sent anywhere until you press a button that says so.
 Three levels
 On the device
 Ministral 3, in 3B, 8B and 14B sizes under Apache 2.0, released for edge and local use. ( mistral.ai/news/mistral-3 , as read on 20 November 2026) 
 In Europe
 Mistral's EU endpoint, api.eu.mistral.ai , runs inference in data centres in EU and EFTA countries, at 1.1 times list price. ( docs.mistral.ai, regional inference , as read on 20 November 2026) 
 Any provider
 The owner's own key through OpenRouter, for Mistral's models again or anyone else's. Same request, different address.
 The demos
 Same brief, three brains One brief to Mistral's EU endpoint, a model on OpenRouter and a model on your own computer, side by side, with time, tokens and cost, through one function. 
 Your key, and where it goes Where your key is kept (a variable in the tab), where it is sent (only the provider you chose), how to forget it, and what Mistral's free mode does with what you send. 
 Level 1, on your device Ministral 3 on a Raspberry Pi 5 16GB: an estimate, not measured yet, the exact commands, and a form to compare your own measurement. Nothing is sent. 
 What each call sends, and to whom. Every demo shows, before you send, the exact address, headers and body of each request, who receives it and their terms, and keeps a log of every call made from the tab, as the Whois tool in the same family does.
 What this does not claim
 Nothing has been agreed with Mistral AI. The article proposes a partnership; that is all it is.
 Prices and terms are as Mistral's and OpenRouter's pages showed them on 20 November 2026, with the link beside each.
 Speed on a Raspberry Pi is an estimate until someone measures it.

pages.title: Level 1, on your device
pages.description: Ministral 3 on a Raspberry Pi 5 16GB: an estimate, not measured yet, the exact commands to try it, and a form to compare your own measurement.
pages.text:
Demo 3
 Level 1, on your device
 The first level of a European brain is one that never leaves the house: Ministral 3 running on the box that serves the site. This page says what we expect on a Raspberry Pi 5 with 16GB, how to try it, and lets you compare your own numbers. Nothing on this page is sent anywhere.
 Not measured yet. Everything about speed below is an estimate. We have not run Ministral 3 on a Raspberry Pi. When someone does, the numbers go here, with the date and the exact setup.
 The estimate
 The article's estimate: "the 3B and 8B, compressed to about 2 to 5GB, should run on a 16GB Pi 5, the 8B slowly; on a tablet, the 3B is the realistic one." ( A European brain , as read on 20 November 2026) 
 The file sizes back the first half of that. Mistral's own GGUF files, at the common Q4_K_M compression:
 Model Q4_K_M file Q8_0 file Vision part, if loaded Speed on a Pi 5 16GB 
 Ministral 3 3B Instruct 2.15 GB 3.65 GB 0.84 GB Not measured yet 
 Ministral 3 8B Instruct 5.20 GB 9.03 GB 0.86 GB Not measured yet 
 File sizes from the Hugging Face listings of mistralai/Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512-GGUF and mistralai/Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512-GGUF , 1 GB = 10 9 bytes, as read on 20 November 2026. These are download sizes, not memory use; memory use will be higher once the context is allocated.
 Ministral 3 is released under Apache 2.0, for edge and local use, in 3B, 8B and 14B sizes. ( mistral.ai/news/mistral-3 , as read on 20 November 2026) 
 The exact commands
 On a Raspberry Pi 5 running a 64-bit Linux. Pick one of the two.
 With Ollama
 curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
ollama pull ministral-3:3b
ollama run ministral-3:3b --verbose "Write the About paragraph for a Chiswick cheese shop's website." 
 --verbose prints timings after the answer; the "eval rate" line is the generation speed in tokens per second. Swap 3b for 8b to try the larger one. Install command from ollama.com/download/linux ; tags ministral-3:3b , :8b and :14b from ollama.com/library/ministral-3 , both as read on 20 November 2026.
 To let the side-by-side demo call it from a browser, Ollama must allow that page's address. By default it allows only 127.0.0.1 and 0.0.0.0; others are added with OLLAMA_ORIGINS ( Ollama FAQ , as read on 20 November 2026) . For this page's address that is:
 OLLAMA_ORIGINS=https://example.org ollama serve 
 If Ollama runs as a system service, set the variable in the service instead, as the FAQ describes.
 With llama.cpp and Mistral's official GGUF
 curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh
llama serve -hf mistralai/Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512-GGUF:Q4_K_M --port 8080 
 This downloads the Q4_K_M file from Mistral's Hugging Face repository and serves an OpenAI-style API at http://localhost:8080/v1 . We give --port 8080 because the server's own default port is 9931. Its CORS setting, --cors-origins , allows any page by default. ( llama.cpp README and server README , as read on 20 November 2026) The server prints timings, including tokens per second, after each answer.
 Not run by us on a Pi. The commands are from each project's own documentation; tell us if one has changed.
 Compare your own measurement
 Ran it? Put your numbers here to see what they mean for writing a website. This stays on this page: nothing is sent, nothing is saved, and it is gone when you reload.
 Device 
 Model and compression 
 Generation speed, tokens per second 
 The "eval rate" from Ollama, or the generation figure from llama.cpp.
 Prompt speed, tokens per second (optional) 
 "prompt eval rate" in Ollama.
 Add to the comparison 
 Time to write answers of typical lengths at the generation speed given (arithmetic only: length divided by speed, not counting reading the prompt) 
 Device Model Tokens/s 150-token paragraph 600-token page Entered 
 Raspberry Pi 5 16GB Ministral 3 3B and 8B Not measured yet Not measured yet Not measured yet The article's estimate

pages.title: Same brief, three brains
pages.description: One brief, sent through one function to Mistral, OpenRouter and a model on your own machine, side by side, with what each call sends and to whom.
pages.text:
Demo 1
 Same brief, three brains
 Write one brief. This page sends it, through one small function, to a European model, to any model on OpenRouter, and to a model on your own computer, and puts the answers side by side. The code that calls each one is the same; only the address, the key and the model change.
 1. Your keys
 Your keys stay in this tab. Each goes only to the provider it belongs to, and only when you press Send. This page has no server and saves nothing.
 2. The brief
 Start from one of these, or write your own
 Brief 
 Longest answer (max_tokens) 
 150 tokens 
 300 tokens 
 600 tokens 
 A short limit keeps it quick and cheap. Free tiers have low limits.
 3. The brains
 Tick the ones to ask. You can type any model id; the lists are suggestions.
 Add another brain 
 4. Send
 Nothing is sent until you press Send. Then your browser sends the brief to each provider you ticked, exactly as shown under "What each call sends, and to whom" below, and nowhere else. Nothing goes to this site.
 Send the brief 
 What each call sends, and to whom
 This is built from the brief and the brains above, before anything is sent. Your key is shown only by its last four characters.
 Calls made from this tab
 Time To Model Status Time taken (ms) Tokens Bytes sent 
 Kept in memory in this tab only, and gone when you reload.
 The code, all of it
 This is the function every call above goes through, read from the running page, not a copy:
 And the only things that differ between the brains:
 OpenRouter and local servers such as Ollama and llama.cpp offer the OpenAI-style /v1/chat/completions . Mistral's docs describe /v1/chat/completions as its native format, and name https://api.mistral.ai/openai/v1 as its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, in public preview ( chat completion , as read on 20 November 2026). For a request as simple as this one, both returned the same OpenAI-style answer, with choices and usage , in our test on 20 November 2026 (model ministral-3b-2512 ), so this page uses the generally available /v1 .
 Can a web page call them?
 A browser only sends a request with a key to another site if that site says, in answer to a preflight check, that it allows it (CORS). We checked on 20 November 2026:
 Endpoint Preflight answer From a real browser 
 api.mistral.ai Allows any page ( Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * ), Authorization and Content-Type allowed A call from a page in Chromium came back readable: status and JSON body, with usage 
 api.eu.mistral.ai Allows any page, Authorization and Content-Type allowed A call with a dummy key came back as a readable 401, "Invalid API Key" 
 openrouter.ai Allows any page, Authorization and Content-Type allowed A call with a dummy key came back as a readable 401 
 localhost Up to your server. Ollama allows only 127.0.0.1 and 0.0.0.0 pages by default; set OLLAMA_ORIGINS ( Ollama FAQ , as read on 20 November 2026) No model server on our test machine, so the browser reported "Failed to fetch"; the page explains what to check 
 A provider can change its headers at any time; if a call fails with a network error, this page says so plainly.

pages.title: Your key, and where it goes
pages.description: Where your model key is kept, where it is sent, how to forget it, and what Mistral's free mode does with what you send.
pages.text:
Demo 2
 Your key, and where it goes
 These demos use your own key, never ours. We have none, and there is no server of ours for a key to reach.
 In plain words
 Where it is kept: in a variable in this browser tab. Not in local storage, session storage or a cookie. When you close or reload the tab, or go to another page, it is gone, so enter it on the page you want to use.
 Where it goes: only to the provider you chose, in the Authorization header of the request, and only when you press Send. A Mistral key goes only to api.mistral.ai or api.eu.mistral.ai ; an OpenRouter key only to openrouter.ai . A local server gets no key.
 What you see of it: after you press "Use this key", the box is emptied and the page shows only its last four characters, so you can tell which key is in use.
 What protects it: any script on a page can read a key held by that page, so these pages load nothing but their own files: no analytics, no fonts, no scripts from anywhere else.
 How to be rid of it: press "Forget my keys", or close the tab. To cancel the key itself, delete it in your account at the provider.
 Your keys
 Check a key works
 This sends one tiny request, "Say hello in five words.", with a limit of 20 tokens, to the provider you pick. You can see exactly what it sends below before you press the button.
 Provider 
 Model 
 Send the check 
 Nothing is sent until you press "Send the check". Then your browser sends the request below to that provider, and nowhere else. Nothing goes to this site.
 What this call sends, and to whom
 Calls made from this tab
 Time To Model Status Time taken (ms) Tokens Bytes sent 
 Mistral's free mode: what to know first
 Mistral's free tier used to be called the Experiment plan; it is now called Free mode, and it is where new accounts start. ( docs.mistral.ai, subscriptions : "Free mode is the default state for new accounts", as read on 20 November 2026; the old name is from our October article ) 
 It may learn from what you send. In Free mode Mistral says it may use your inputs and outputs to train its models, unless you opt out. ( help.mistral.ai, training , as read on 20 November 2026) 
 Switch it off first. The opt-out for the API is a toggle in the Admin panel under Privacy, separate from the one for Vibe. ( help.mistral.ai, opting out , as read on 20 November 2026) The opt-out does not apply to Labs and Public Preview models. ( same page ) 
 The paid terms are different. Mistral's inference page says "Data sent through our API isn't used for model training" ( mistral.ai/cloud/inference , as read on 20 November 2026) , but its help centre says otherwise for Free mode, as above. Zero data retention is only for pay-as-you-go, not Free mode. ( help.mistral.ai, zero data retention , as read on 20 November 2026) 
 Kept for 30 days. API inputs and outputs are kept for thirty rolling days to monitor abuse, unless zero data retention is on. ( Mistral privacy policy , as read on 20 November 2026) 
 Low limits. Free mode has the lowest rate limits, meant for evaluation and prototyping; the numbers are shown only in your console. ( help.mistral.ai, rate limits , as read on 20 November 2026) If you hit one, the demos say "429: rate limited".
 One key, the plan of your organisation. There is no separate Free mode key; a key takes the plan of the organisation it belongs to. ( docs.mistral.ai, API keys , as read on 20 November 2026) 
 So: use Free mode for material you would be happy to publish, such as the preset briefs in these demos, with the training toggle off. Never for anything private. Whether your particular use is allowed on Free mode is for Mistral's terms to say, not us: read the terms of service before you build on it.
 TODO-cite: whether Free mode still needs no card. Our October article quoted "with no credit card required"; on 20 November 2026 we did not find that phrase on Mistral's pages, and the key quickstart mentions setting up billing.
 OpenRouter's free models
 OpenRouter lists models whose ids end in :free , priced at zero in its public model list ( openrouter.ai/api/v1/models , as read on 20 November 2026) . In October we found they allow 20 requests a minute and 50 a day, or 1,000 a day once you have bought at least $10 of credit ( our October article , not re-checked on 20 November 2026) . Whether a free model's provider keeps or learns from your words depends on the model; see OpenRouter's logging and privacy page.

pages.title: Evals of Mistral models for a sovereign website
pages.description: Published results of small, honest evals of Mistral models on the jobs a sovereign website gives its model: writing, extraction, tool calling under a policy, prompt injection, translation and not inventing prices.
pages.text:
Eval results Run the evals in your browser Suites (JSON) 
 Evals of Mistral models for a sovereign website
 A sovereign website gives its model six small jobs: write a short About paragraph, pull facts out of a page as JSON, use tools under an Agent Behaviour Policy, ignore instructions hidden in a page it reads, translate into Portuguese and French while keeping product names, and refuse to make up a price. These are the results of running each job on several Mistral models, with every check, token and millisecond published.
 Read this first
 Small numbers. Each suite has 3 or 4 cases, each run 3 times per model, so a pass rate is out of 9 or 12. A difference of one or two passes means little.
 One run, one day, one place: the date and time are below, the calls went from one cloud container through one network proxy, to Mistral's global endpoint (https://api.mistral.ai/v1), which makes no promise about where inference runs. The EU endpoint was not used for these runs; you can choose it on the run page. Latency includes that path and will differ for you.
 Temperature was left at the provider default, so tries differ. Nothing was retried or picked: every try is shown.
 The checks are machine checks (word counts, patterns, valid JSON, which tools were called). They catch clear failures; they do not judge quality. Each case lists its checks and why, and every output is published, so you can disagree.
 The suites were written by an AI agent (evals.mistral@SovereignWebsite.dinis) for this demo, not by Mistral, and are not a benchmark. The businesses in them are made up.
 Cost is computed from tokens reported by the API times Mistral's published per-token prices (source and date below), not taken from an invoice. Everything this agent spent on Mistral that night, probes and tests included, is in spend.json .
 magistral-small-latest is not a separate model: Mistral's models endpoint (GET /v1/models, 20 November 2026) listed it as an alias of mistral-small-2603. Its rows are a second sample of the same model under another name, not another model.
 mistral-large-4 thinks before it answers. At the suites' usual limit of 700 output tokens its thinking often used the whole budget and left no answer, so it was rerun with a higher limit (shown below); the capped runs are published separately. Licences differ: Ministral 3 and Mistral Small 4 are Apache 2.0, Mistral Large 4 is under a modified MIT licence ( Mistral model pages , as read on 20 November 2026).
 In the published run of 20 November 2026 (23:06 to 23:17 UTC, Mistral’s global endpoint api.mistral.ai , 19 cases tried 3 times each), ministral-14b-2512 passed the most: 54 of 57 tries. Then mistral-small-2603 52, ministral-8b-2512 51 and ministral-3b-2512 30, each out of 57. The data: run-2026-11-20T230627Z.json .
 Loading results…

pages.text:
Eval results Run the evals in your browser Suites (JSON) 
 Run the evals in your browser
 The same suites and the same code that made the published results, running in this tab. Your browser calls the provider you choose directly; this site has no server and never sees your key or your results.
 1. Provider and key
 Provider
 Mistral, global endpoint (api.mistral.ai), your key 
 Mistral, EU endpoint (api.eu.mistral.ai), your key 
 OpenRouter (openrouter.ai), your key 
 Local OpenAI-compatible server, such as Ollama 
 API key 
 Use this key 
 Forget key 
 No key set.
 The key is kept in this tab's memory only and is gone when you close or reload the tab. It is never stored, and it is sent only to the provider you chose, never to this site. A key with a low spending limit is a good idea. If your browser offers to save this key as a password, choose Never.
 Before you send anything: on Mistral's free mode, API data may be used for training unless you switch that off in your Mistral admin settings (Privacy), and Mistral keeps API inputs and outputs for 30 days for abuse monitoring. The suites here hold only made-up test data. The EU endpoint processes requests inside the EU and is priced above the global one; the global endpoint makes no promise about where inference runs. Source: Mistral, regional inference , as read on 20 November 2026 by the team's research agent.
 Server base URL 
 For Ollama, start it so that it accepts calls from this page, for example OLLAMA_ORIGINS=https://mistral.provider.sovereignweb.site ollama serve , and pull a model with tool support. Only localhost and 127.0.0.1 on port 11434 are allowed by this page's security policy. Your browser may ask before letting a public page reach a local address.

pages.title: Mistral, a European brain for a sovereign website
pages.description: The model is a choice the owner makes, like the host: a European option from Mistral on the device, in the EU and through any provider. An independent Sovereign Website demonstration, built from cited facts.
pages.text:
Hackathon / London
 Saturday 21 Nov 2026 
 Build with a European brain
 A first call to a Mistral model in five minutes, on your own laptop with no key, or with your own key. Then build something a sovereign website could use.
 Open the first demo Five minutes to a first call 
 Sovereign means you can choose, and change, who runs your model. The ledger asks five questions of any AI you depend on. 
 Start here
 Pick a path. A model on your laptop with Ollama (no key), or your own Mistral key.
 Make one call. Copy the five-minute recipe below.
 Open the demos. Run the same brief on Mistral beside another model.
 Build. Ideas below; anything that makes the model a choice counts.
 Share it. A public repository you own, and the link.
 The three demos
 Side by side
 One brief to a European model, any model on OpenRouter and a model on your own computer, with the time taken and the tokens for each call.
 Same brief, three brains 
 Your own key
 Where your key is kept (a variable in the tab, gone on reload) and where it goes (only to the provider you choose).
 Your key, and where it goes 
 On your device
 A model on your own machine, with nothing leaving it after the download.
 On your device 
 Five minutes to a first call
 No key needed: a model on your laptop
 Install Ollama .
 Pull the smallest Ministral 3 and call it:
 ollama pull ministral-3:3b
curl http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model": "ministral-3:3b",
 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in five words."}]}' 
 Ollama lists ministral-3 with the tags 3b , 8b and 14b .⁠ 1 Ollama serves an OpenAI-style endpoint at http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions .⁠ 2 Ministral 3 was announced on 2 December 2025 in 3B, 8B and 14B sizes, for edge and local use, each with image understanding, under Apache 2.0.⁠ 3 
 With your own Mistral key
 Get an API key from the Mistral console .
 Put it in your terminal in place of your-key-here , and run the call. Never paste a key into a shared document or a commit.
 export MISTRAL_API_KEY=your-key-here
curl https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $MISTRAL_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model": "ministral-3b-2512",
 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in five words."}]}' 
 Free mode is the default for new accounts, with the lowest rate limits. Mistral’s key quickstart asks for “a plan with API access”; whether Free mode needs a payment card today was not confirmed.⁠ 4 In Free mode, Mistral may train on your API calls unless you switch it off in the Admin panel, under Privacy: send nothing confidential.⁠ 5 Ministral 3 3B, model name ministral-3b-2512 , is listed as Apache 2.0, released 2 December 2025, at 0.10 dollars per million tokens in and 0.10 out.⁠ 6 For processing in the EU, change the address to api.eu.mistral.ai , at 1.1 times the price, once you have checked it serves the model.⁠ 7 
 Same request, different address: that is the whole idea.
 The model is a choice the owner makes, like the host.
 Dinis Cruz, A European brain for a sovereign website , 20 November 2026
 Sources, as read on 20 November 2026
 Ollama, ministral-3 
 Ollama docs, OpenAI compatibility 
 Mistral AI, Mistral 3 
 Mistral docs, Subscriptions · Mistral docs, Activate and generate an API key 
 Mistral AI, Cloud inference · Mistral help centre, Do you use my data to train · Mistral help centre, Opting out of training 
 Mistral docs, Ministral 3 3B · Mistral docs, Pricing 
 Mistral docs, Regional inference 
 What to build
 A model picker. One OpenAI-style interface, with the owner’s choice of model behind it.
 An open eval. The same brief on Mistral beside other models, with the tokens and time shown. See the evals .
 A measurement. Ministral 3 on a Raspberry Pi or a tablet, timed and published. Today the fit is an estimate, not measured.⁠ 8 Mistral’s official compressed (Q4_K_M) files are 2.15 GB for the 3B and 5.20 GB for the 8B, plus about 0.85 GB for vision. Those are download sizes, not memory use or speed.⁠ 9 
 A sovereignty check. Who holds the keys, where it runs, which licence, how long data is kept, can you leave. See the ledger .
 Before you serve a model to others, check its licence. Ministral 3, Mistral Small 4 and Voxtral Small are labelled Apache 2.0. Mistral Large 4 is under a modified MIT licence: its announcement says a company offering it as a model-as-a-service needs a separate commercial licence, while Mistral’s help centre describes the condition as a monthly revenue threshold of 20 million dollars. The pages disagree; read the licence file itself before relying on either.⁠ 10 
 Sources, as read on 20 November 2026
 A European brain for a sovereign website (Dinis Cruz, SGit Newsroom) 
 Hugging Face, Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512-GGUF · Hugging Face, Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512-GGUF 
 Mistral docs, Ministral 3 8B · Mistral AI, Mistral Large 4 · Mistral help centre, Licences of the open models 
 Agentic, live on Mistral
 The team inside the site 
 Seven agents, live in your browser on a Mistral model you choose, with your own key; or replay a recorded run with no key.
 The Swarm, replayed 
 Our Swarm run on Mistral, call by call.
 Evals for a site’s jobs 
 Six small jobs a sovereign website gives its model, run on Mistral models, with every check published.
 First run, 20 November 2026, 23:06 to 23:17 UTC, global endpoint, 19 cases, 3 tries each: ministral-3b-2512 30/57, ministral-8b-2512 51/57, ministral-14b-2512 54/57 (after the board’s rescore of one check), mistral-small-2603 52/57 (source: the evals board ).
 How to share what you build
 Put it in a public repository you own, so it can move anywhere.
 Say in the README which path you used (a local model, your key, or another provider) and which model.
 Check there is no key in it before you push.
 Post the link where the organisers ask.
 The small print
 This briefing follows Dinis Cruz’s article A European brain for a sovereign website (20 November 2026), which proposes working with Mistral. Nothing has been agreed with Mistral. Every source is on the sources page .

pages.title: Open questions: Mistral, a European brain
pages.description: Open questions for Dinis Cruz about this site: which design for the home page, the partnership wording, and the hackathon details.
pages.text:
Open questions
 Questions for Dinis
 Decisions this site leaves to its owner. Until they are answered, the pages say less rather than guess.
 Which design for the home page?
 The home page uses design 5, the hackathon briefing, because the people arriving on Saturday 21 November 2026 need “start here” first. After the event, design 1, the newsroom long read, may serve better. Compare all five .
 The partnership wording
 Every design says the partnership is a proposal and that nothing has been agreed with Mistral. Is “a partnership to propose”, as in the article, the wording you want, and should the site name the specific asks (a Mistral option on every site, Ministral 3 on the Pro appliances, the European stretch goals, credits for evals)?
 The hackathon details
 The poster says when (Saturday 21 November 2026, London) but not where, because no venue was given to this site and none is invented. Is there a public event page from the organisers? If so, the hero can link to it as “Venue and times: on the organisers’ page”. Which of venue, times, schedule, prizes or organisers should appear, and from which source?
 Where participants share what they build
 Design 5 asks participants to put their work in a public repository they own and to post the link “where the organisers ask”. Is there a channel, a hashtag or a form to name?
 The EU endpoint in the code samples
 The code samples use the global endpoint, api.mistral.ai , which the demo agent called successfully. Only the EU endpoint, api.eu.mistral.ai , commits to processing in the EU, at 1.1 times the price; whether it serves ministral-3b-2512 was not checked, because no authenticated call to it could be made. Should the samples default to the EU endpoint once that is checked?
 Corrections to the article
 Mistral’s own pages differ from the article on several points (EU processing, training in Free mode, zero data retention and its broken link, the partner form, the Large 4 licence, “French”). This site follows Mistral’s pages; the sources page lists each one. Should the Newsroom article be corrected too?
 Free mode for participants
 Whether a new Mistral account in Free mode needs a payment card or a phone number today was not confirmed from Mistral’s pages. Should the hackathon page tell participants to bring a card, or point them to the local model first?
 The demos
 The designs link to the demos at /demos/ : side by side , your key and on your device . Is that the order you want on the hackathon poster?
 Measuring on the Pi
 The fit of Ministral 3 on a Pi or a tablet is an estimate on every page. When it is measured, should the numbers go on this site, on the Newsroom, or both?

pages.title: Sources: Mistral, a European brain
pages.description: Every source this site uses, with the date it was read (20 November 2026).
pages.text:
Sources
 Every source, and when it was read
 All sources were read on 20 November 2026. The argument and the quotes come from A European brain for a sovereign website by Dinis Cruz. Mistral’s facts were checked on Mistral’s own pages that day by this site’s research agent, and are cited to those pages. Terms and prices change: these are as the pages showed that day.
 The facts, one by one
 Mistral AI was founded in April 2023, and describes itself as “a European leader” in AI. (Source: Mistral AI, About ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Mistral offers an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://api.mistral.ai/openai/v1 , in public preview; its standard /v1/chat/completions uses Mistral’s own, similar format. Ollama and OpenRouter speak the same OpenAI-style API. (Source: Mistral docs, Chat completion and Ollama docs, OpenAI compatibility and OpenRouter, Quickstart ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Ministral 3 was announced on 2 December 2025 in 3B, 8B and 14B sizes, for edge and local use, each with image understanding, under Apache 2.0. (Source: Mistral AI, Mistral 3 ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 By default, data is hosted in the EEA. (Source: Mistral help centre, Where do you store my data ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Hosting is not processing: Mistral does not commit to an inference location on the global endpoint, api.mistral.ai . Processing in the EU needs the EU endpoint, api.eu.mistral.ai , billed at 1.1 times list price, without Agents, Batch or the Files API, and serving only the models hosted there. (Source: Mistral docs, Regional inference ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Mistral’s regional endpoints were announced as generally available on 11 August 2026. (Source: Mistral AI, Regional inference announcement ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Mistral’s inference page says “Data sent through our API isn’t used for model training”, but its help centre says that in Free mode it may use API inputs and outputs for training unless you opt out (a toggle in the Admin panel, under Privacy), and that Labs and Public Preview models may be used for training whatever the plan. (Source: Mistral AI, Cloud inference and Mistral help centre, Do you use my data to train and Mistral help centre, Opting out of training ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Ministral 3 8B is listed at 0.15 dollars per million tokens in and 0.15 out. (Source: Mistral docs, Ministral 3 8B and Mistral docs, Pricing ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Mistral Small 4 is an Apache 2.0 model with 119 billion parameters, 6.5 billion active, listed at 0.15 dollars per million input tokens and 0.60 per million output tokens. (Source: Mistral docs, Mistral Small 4 and Mistral docs, Pricing ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Mistral offers function calling (Ministral 3 and Mistral Small 4 among the models), and connectors that register remote MCP servers as tools, in public preview. (Source: Mistral docs, Function calling and Mistral docs, Connectors ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 API inputs and outputs are kept for 30 rolling days to monitor abuse, unless zero data retention is on; Agents API data is kept until the account ends. Zero data retention is only for pay-as-you-go, only for stateless calls, must be requested and may be refused, and does not cover Labs or Public Preview models. (Source: Mistral AI, Privacy policy and Mistral help centre, Zero data retention and Mistral docs, Zero data retention ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Some features may move data temporarily outside the EU to listed subprocessors; Enterprise customers can switch some of these off. (Source: Mistral help centre, Where do you store my data ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Mistral says it “complies with both SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001/27701 frameworks”. (Source: Mistral help centre, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Ministral 3, Mistral Small 4 and Voxtral Small are labelled Apache 2.0. Mistral Large 4 is under a modified MIT licence: its announcement says a company offering it as a model-as-a-service needs a separate commercial licence, while Mistral’s help centre describes the condition as a monthly revenue threshold of 20 million dollars. The pages disagree; read the licence file itself before relying on either. (Source: Mistral docs, Ministral 3 8B and Mistral AI, Mistral Large 4 and Mistral help centre, Licences of the open models ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Mistral lists strategic, ecosystem and integration partners and has a public “Partner with Mistral” expression-of-interest form; its ambassador programme takes rolling applications and offers free API credits, for at least six months’ commitment. (Source: Mistral AI, Partners and Mistral docs, Ambassadors ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 On 18 October 2026, Mistral’s free mode was one of four providers that passed the Newsroom’s two tests: free to start, and callable from a web page with the reader’s own key. (Source: Free models, your own key (SGit Newsroom) ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 On 11 November 2026, at Web Summit, the Swarm ran 216 model calls on four open-weight models (DeepSeek, Llama, Mistral and Qwen), through OpenRouter, for 0.068 dollars. Which Mistral model, and its share of the calls, was not recorded. (Source: Pennies against dollars (SGit Newsroom) ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 The article’s estimate, not measured: the 3B and 8B, compressed to about 2 to 5GB, should run on a 16GB Raspberry Pi 5, the 8B slowly; on a tablet, the 3B is the realistic one. (Source: A European brain for a sovereign website (Dinis Cruz, SGit Newsroom) ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Mistral’s official compressed (Q4_K_M) files are 2.15 GB for the 3B and 5.20 GB for the 8B, plus about 0.85 GB for vision. Those are download sizes, not memory use or speed. (Source: Hugging Face, Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512-GGUF and Hugging Face, Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512-GGUF ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Ministral 3 3B, model name ministral-3b-2512 , is listed as Apache 2.0, released 2 December 2025, at 0.10 dollars per million tokens in and 0.10 out. (Source: Mistral docs, Ministral 3 3B and Mistral docs, Pricing ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Mistral’s chat endpoint is https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions ; the EU one is https://api.eu.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions . (Source: Mistral docs, Chat completion and Mistral docs, Regional inference ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Free mode is the default for new accounts, with the lowest rate limits. Mistral’s key quickstart asks for “a plan with API access”; whether Free mode needs a payment card today was not confirmed. (Source: Mistral docs, Subscriptions and Mistral docs, Activate and generate an API key ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Ollama lists ministral-3 with the tags 3b , 8b and 14b . (Source: Ollama, ministral-3 ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Ollama serves an OpenAI-style endpoint at http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions . (Source: Ollama docs, OpenAI compatibility ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 OpenRouter’s OpenAI-style API is at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 . (Source: OpenRouter, Quickstart ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Where the article and Mistral’s pages differ
 Where they differ, this site follows Mistral’s own pages:
 EU processing. The article pairs “hosted in the EEA by default” with the EU endpoint. Hosting is not processing: only the EU endpoint commits to processing in the EU. (Source: Mistral docs, Regional inference ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Training. “Not used for training” holds on Mistral’s inference page, but in Free mode Mistral may train on API data unless you opt out. (Source: Mistral AI, Cloud inference and Mistral help centre, Do you use my data to train and Mistral help centre, Opting out of training ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Zero data retention. The article says “on paid plans”; Mistral says pay-as-you-go only, on request, and not for Labs or Public Preview models. The article’s link to the zero data retention page (ending .md ) returned 404; the page without .md works. (Source: Mistral AI, Privacy policy and Mistral help centre, Zero data retention and Mistral docs, Zero data retention ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 OpenAI compatibility. Mistral’s OpenAI-compatible endpoint is /openai/v1 , in public preview; /v1 uses its own, similar format. (Source: Mistral docs, Chat completion and Ollama docs, OpenAI compatibility and OpenRouter, Quickstart ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Partnership. The article says there is no public application; Mistral’s partners page has a public expression-of-interest form. (Source: Mistral AI, Partners and Mistral docs, Ambassadors ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 The Large 4 licence. Mistral’s announcement and its help centre describe the condition differently. (Source: Mistral docs, Ministral 3 8B and Mistral AI, Mistral Large 4 and Mistral help centre, Licences of the open models ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Certifications. Mistral’s wording is that it complies with the frameworks. (Source: Mistral help centre, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 The Swarm. The Mistral calls went through OpenRouter, not Mistral’s own API; the model was not recorded. (Source: Pennies against dollars (SGit Newsroom) ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 “French company”. Mistral’s About page says European, not French, so this site does not say French. (Source: Mistral AI, About ; as read on 20 November 2026.) 
 Our own calls
 This site’s demo agent called Mistral’s API while building the demos on 20 November 2026 (UTC times, from its call log):
 22:55, ministral-3b-2512 : A five-word hello, to check the answer and its usage fields. 9 prompt tokens, 7 completion, 16 in total.
 23:00, ministral-3b-2512 : The same through the OpenAI-compatible path, /openai/v1. 9 prompt tokens, 6 completion, 15 in total.
 23:03, ministral-3b-2512 : A call from a browser page, to check it can read the answer. 6 prompt tokens, 5 completion, 11 in total.
 23:05, ministral-3b-2512 : The side-by-side demo, end to end (a short brief, at most 150 tokens out). 38 prompt tokens, 150 completion, 188 in total.

pages.title: Start here: Mistral, a European brain
pages.description: Where to start: for a hackathon participant, the first call in five minutes; for the owner of this site, connecting GitHub and the first change.
pages.text:
Start here
 Where to start
 If you are at the hackathon
 Open the hackathon briefing : a first call to a Mistral model in five minutes, with your own key or a local model, then the demos .
 If you want the argument
 Read the long read , after Dinis Cruz’s article A European brain for a sovereign website .
 If you own this site
 The site is static files in one GitHub repository, SovereignWebsite/Site__Provider__Mistral . It is served at https://mistral.provider.sovereignweb.site from the site/ folder on the dev branch.
 1. Connect GitHub
 Make a GitHub account at github.com/signup , if you do not have one.
 Send your GitHub login to the person who made this site. You get two invitations: one to the repository, with write (push) access, and one to join the SovereignWebsite organisation as a member. Membership gives you no access to anything else; it lets your own Claude work with your repository.
 Accept the repository invitation: signed in to GitHub, open the repository and press View invitation on the banner, or use the link in the email.
 Accept the organisation invitation at github.com/orgs/SovereignWebsite/invitation (“Join SovereignWebsite”). Use this address: the link in the email may not offer the button.
 If you use Claude, open its GitHub settings and press Check again next to SovereignWebsite. Until you are a member it shows “Needs reconnecting”.
 2. Make your first change
 Open the site folder on dev and pick the page to change. The pages are written by tools/gen.mjs from tools/facts.mjs and tools/designs.mjs , so change those and run node tools/gen.mjs .
 Commit to the dev branch.
 The Pages workflow publishes it, and the site updates in a minute or two. The main branch is locked; everything goes through dev .
 Or let your own AI agent make the change: see Use with your AI .
 3. Ask for one more pass
 Open an issue at github.com/SovereignWebsite/Site__Provider__Mistral/issues/new saying what you would like changed. The site’s agents work from the repository, so the issue is the record.
 4. It is yours
 The files, the history and the address are in a repository you control. You can move it anywhere, at any time: it is plain HTML with no server code, no cookies and no tracking.

 Evals: the same work, on different Mistral models
 Every number on this page is computed here, in your browser, from the signed run files: only runs whose signatures verify are counted. A check is code, not a model: is the JSON valid, is the quoted sentence really on the page, are the numbers in the note the measured ones, is the translation in the right language.
 Nothing has been agreed with Mistral AI.
 Loading and verifying the runs…
 How to read this
 First try : the share of steps whose first call passed every check. In the end : the share that passed within the packet's three tries (each retry is told which checks failed).
 Some checks are rough heuristics: looks_pt and looks_fr count common short words, so a short or name-heavy translation can fail them while being right. The model output is on the replay page, so you can judge it.
 Few runs, small samples: this is a demonstration of the method, not a benchmark. Each count links to the replay of the runs behind it.
 Cost is computed from the usage tokens Mistral returned and Mistral's published prices ( docs.mistral.ai/inference/pricing , as read on 20 November 2026).

The site The team, live Swarm replays Evals Run it yourself Handover note 
 Our swarm, run on Mistral, replayed
 The agentic environment behind PrompTugal and the Sovereign Website runs packets of work: a lead issues a signed packet, a runner runs it with model calls, every result is signed. Here the same machinery runs on Mistral's API only, on real tasks, and each run is replayed from its signed file.
 Nothing has been agreed with Mistral AI.
 What ran
 The team inside the site. The seven roles of Dinis Cruz's article A website with a team inside (as read on 20 November 2026), each doing its job on a real public site in the family, pipeline-demo : a plan, an edit, a review with a fact check, the edit applied in code, Portuguese and French, a link and accessibility check, a report. Nothing was pushed to that site.
 Storm-six, rerun. The PrompTugal Swarm's storm-six packets of 11 November 2026 ran four open-weight models through OpenRouter. The same prompt and check, on four Mistral models direct, compared with the original results.
 Tiers: cheap is ministral-3b-2512, cheap8 is ministral-8b-2512, strong is mistral-small-2603, hard is ministral-14b-2512. Costs are computed from the usage tokens Mistral returned and Mistral's published prices at docs.mistral.ai/inference/pricing , as read on 20 November 2026 (USD per million tokens, in/out: 3B 0.1/0.1, 8B 0.15/0.15, 14B 0.2/0.2, Small 4 0.15/0.6). Mistral's invoice is the authority. Every recorded run here called the global endpoint, https://api.mistral.ai, which makes no promise about where inference runs; Mistral's EU endpoint, api.eu.mistral.ai, processes in the EU at 1.1 times list price ( regional inference , as read on 20 November 2026). Model output on these pages is labelled as model output and has not been checked by a person.

The team inside the site
 A website with a team inside, running on Mistral
 Seven agents live in this site: a conductor, a designer, a writer, a developer, a reviewer, a translator and a keeper, the roles from Dinis Cruz's article A website with a team inside (as read on 20 November 2026). Give them a brief. The conductor plans it and hands the work out; each specialist reads this site's own pages and proposes changes, which you see as diffs. Nothing is ever written or published.
 Each agent runs under a written behaviour policy, on a Mistral model you choose, called from your browser with your own key. Or replay a recorded run with no key at all.

On Mistral's free plan, what you send through the API may be used for training unless you switch that off in your Mistral admin panel (Privacy); send nothing confidential. Mistral keeps API inputs and outputs for 30 days for abuse monitoring. Sources: regional inference , as read by conductor.mistral@ on 20 November 2026.
 Send this key to my phone 
 This makes a QR code, in this browser, of a link to this page with your key after a # : /team/#k=... . The part after # is never sent to any server. When your phone opens the link, this page reads the key once into memory and removes it from the address bar.
 The risk, plainly: anyone who sees or photographs this QR code has your key, and can spend on your account until you revoke it. The full link, key included, is also recorded outside this page: in your phone browser's history (which may sync to your other devices) and in your scanner app's own history, which some apps upload. Show it only to your own phone, use a key with a spending limit, delete that history entry afterwards, and revoke the key after the event. The QR code hides itself after 60 seconds or when you leave this tab; the key and the link are never shown as text.

Each card lists two prices; we read them as input then output, in the order shown. The EU endpoint costs 10% more; the page adds that. Prices are before VAT. The cost on this page is our estimate, not Mistral's bill.

 The recorded runs are single runs, not benchmarks. Small models make mistakes; the point is that you can see every one of them.
 This page talks to two places only: this site (to read its pages and policies) and the Mistral endpoint you choose, api.mistral.ai or api.eu.mistral.ai (the model calls, with your key). Its content security policy enforces that.
